name: Hadithi Haramu — The Forbidden Story Feed
creator: Collective origin; attributed to founding operator 'Breckenridge Osei-Falcão'
description: A pirate neural broadcast operating out of rotating the Gray Zone-side relay nodes throughout the lower Stack, Hadithi Haramu — Swahili for 'forbidden story' — pushes raw, unvetted testimony directly into BCI feeds of subscribers who have accepted an unsigned trust certificate, bypassing corponation content filters entirely. Broadcasts are irregular, sometimes daily, sometimes silent for weeks, and consist of first-person witness accounts, leaked corporate documents read aloud, intercepted internal comms, and occasional live audio from restricted zones. The production quality is deliberately rough — ambient the Gray Zone noise, breath, background static — because the collective views polish as a mark of corporate contamination.
medium: pirate neural feed (unsanctioned BCI injection), occasional legacy FM radio bleed for unaugmented the Gray Zone residents
cultural_impact: Hadithi Haramu has broken at least four major stories later confirmed by investigative outlets — including early evidence of the 2213 the Gray Zone water crisis later suppressed by Kumbukumbu Live — and has become a primary trust source for Tier 1 communities who regard all licensed broadcast as corponation theater.
controversy: Meridian Broadcast Authority has issued seven suppression orders since 2207, none fully effective; in 2215 a suspected relay operator, Tomé Brandt-Achebe, was arrested and held under the Corponation Communications Security Act for eighteen months without charge, which tripled the feed's subscriber base. Ongoing debate within the collective about whether accepting outside funding from a Tier 3 civil liberties org would compromise editorial independence has caused at least one internal schism.
story_hooks: A character receives an unsolicited Hadithi Haramu transmission containing their own name — and details of something they did that no one should know.
The collective's current relay operator wants out, and the only person they trust to hand the infrastructure to is someone who works for a corponation — even if sympathetically.
A corporate fixer is tasked not with shutting down Hadithi Haramu but with quietly planting one false story to permanently discredit it — and needs a believable insider to deliver it.
